description.narrative:
Key results to be achieved in Morocco, Tunisia, Egypt, Jordan: • Young women and men have enhanced employability and engage in entrepreneurship • Small and medium enterprises and entrepreneurships grow and create jobs through development of innovative solutions, scaling up of existing solutions and improved access to finance and technical assistance • Human Rights are promoted and protected for and by youth through a systemic approach involving all human rights stakeholders, youth networks and youth alliances in support of reform efforts • Violence and torture targeting youth is prevented, free media is strengthened and gender equality is improved through legislative reform, capacity building and dialogue
Justification for support: • DAPP is aligned with Danish foreign policy interests in the region. DAPP is based on lessons learned from past programmes • DAPP seeks to address the root causes of migration by creating better lives for young people through programmes that support human rights, inclusion and employment generation • DAPP’s Human Rights Based Approach will be continued and amplified as it has demonstrated good results • DAPP has a longstanding presence in the region, that has fostered well-established and successful cooperation between Danish and local partners
Major risks and challenges: • Increasing political instability with potential for civil unrest will be addressed by monitoring the situation and taking appropriate action in close collaboration with partners. • Worsening economic situation and potential for increased poverty and migration will be mitigated by the DAPP focus on economic and social exclusion of youth. • Increasing authoritarian rule, repression of minorities, and abuse of power will be addressed by engaging with both human rights duty bearers and right holders.

actual.value:
Indicator 1.2.1: Academic and Internship Support to ArMa Programme
Sub-indicator 1.2.1a: Completion of Masters Degrees and Internships
Achievement:
The target was for at least 20 students from DAPP focus countries to complete a masters degree in human rights and democracy, and for at least one ArMa student to have an internship at a HRIC local office or partners office. According to the annual report, 22 students from DAPP focus countries successfully completed their masters degrees in human rights and democracy, exceeding the target. Additionally, two ArMa students secured internships at HRIC local offices or partner offices, meeting and exceeding the internship target. Sub-indicator 1.2.1b: Modules and Seminars Designed and Delivered by DIHR
Achievement:
The target was for ArMa students to receive one course/module on international human rights mechanisms and the national human rights system, and one seminar on relevant contemporary issues designed and delivered by DIHR. The report indicates that DIHR successfully designed and delivered two modules and one seminar. The modules covered international human rights mechanisms and the national human rights system, while the seminar addressed contemporary issues such as global health, human rights, and technology. The feedback from the students on these educational interventions was positive, indicating a significant increase in their knowledge and capacity in these areas. Indicator 1.2.2: Strengthening ArMa Programmes Organisational Capacity
Achievement:
The target involved evidence of enhanced organisational capacity of the ArMa Programme, which includes the implementation of upgraded or new procedures, and an increase in the number of enrolled students from the DAPP focus countries. The report highlights several enhancements in the organisational capacity of the ArMa Programme: New administrative procedures were implemented to streamline operations and improve the overall management of the programme. Student evaluations indicated improved satisfaction with the programmes structure and content. The number of enrolled students from DAPP focus countries increased by 15%, reflecting the programmes growing attractiveness and capacity to accommodate more students.

actual.value:
Indicator 1.1.1 Number of Regional Courses and Seminars Organized
Achievement The annual report indicates that multiple regional courses and seminars have been successfully organized for state actors with a human rights mandate. These events have included participation from governmental human rights focal points and National Human Rights Institutions (NHRIs), along with key regional actors. The courses and seminars specifically addressed human rights concerns relevant to the MENA region, fulfilling the objective of enhancing the capacity of state actors to perform their human rights mandates effectively. Details regarding the exact number and nature of these courses are included in the detailed sections of the report, confirming the successful organization and implementation of these educational initiatives. Indicator 1.1.2 Peer-to-Peer Exchanges and Regional Cooperation
Sub-indicator 1.1.2a Completion of Master's Degrees
Achievement At least 75 students from the MENA region have completed a masters degree in Human Rights and Democratization. This achievement highlights the success of educational programs aimed at building a knowledgeable base of human rights professionals in the region. The completion of these degrees by a significant number of students indicates a robust academic support system and the effectiveness of the program in meeting its educational targets. Sub-indicator 1.1.2b Peer-to-Peer Exchanges
Achievement: Numerous peer-to-peer exchanges have been organized, facilitating knowledge sharing and the exchange of best practices among governmental human rights focal points, NHRIs, and other key regional actors. These exchanges have provided valuable opportunities for participants to learn from each others experiences and to develop more effective strategies for addressing human rights issues in their respective contexts. Sub-indicator 1.1.2c: Evidence of Effective Regional Cooperation and Coordination
Achievement: There is documented evidence of effective regional cooperation and coordination involving key regional actors, such as the Arab Network for NHRIs. Joint initiatives and capacity-building interventions have been undertaken to enhance the human rights knowledge and capacity of state actors. Specific examples of these cooperative efforts are detailed in the report, showcasing successful collaborations that have led to improved human rights practices and systems within the region.
